text:
acme_dev: Hey team — we've got a production regression on embeddings: p99 for /v1/embeddings jumped from ~220ms to ~1.8s intermittently over the last 3 hours. It correlates with large batched requests from our ingestion workers. Also seeing occasional 400s with 'dimension mismatch'.

jen_support: Sorry you're hitting this, can you paste a recent request and the error payload? Also what model are you calling and max_batch_size config?

acme_dev: Here's a stripped repro payload (we send these at scale, batched):

```json
{
  "model": "open-embed-xlarge",
  "input": ["hello world", "foo", "bar", ...],
  "metadata": {"client_id": "acme-01"}
}
```

Error log we captured: `ERROR embedding_worker: Dim mismatch: expected 1024 got 1536 for request batch_id=cb-7f9`. Intermittent 400s. Most requests succeed.

ryan_ml: That dim mismatch indicates we're batching inputs that target different model variants (1024 vs 1536 dims). Are you sure all clients are consistently calling the same model version? Any chance some calls are routed to a quantized/faq variant?

acme_dev: All clients call `open-embed-xlarge` by name. We recently rolled out a canary for `open-embed-xlarge:v2` that uses a 1536 dim checkpoint — could that be mixing? Our SDK sets model name only.

alex_sre: Likely explanation: smart routing + dynbatch coalescing combined requests across model variants when the routing key isn't enforced. If a worker pool has mixed pinned model variants, dynamic batching could coalesce across them and then the runtime fails on KV cache/dim consistency. I saw similar when routing policy allowed fallback by alias.

jen_support: For immediate mitigation try: 1) set `max_batch_size` lower for that model route (e.g., 8) or temporarily disable dynamic batching for embeddings, 2) ensure model alias is pinned (use fully-qualified model id `open-embed-xlarge:v1`), 3) add a client-side check for vector dim after embed call (defensive).

acme_dev: How do we disable dynbatch per-route? We don't want a global change.

ryan_ml: In the console -> Models -> Route config -> Advanced -> Dynamic batching: toggle off, or via API: `PATCH /routes/{route_id}` with payload `{ "dynamic_batching": false }`. Also you can set `route.max_batch_size` and `route.batch_key` (use `client_id` or `request_id`) to avoid coalescing across tenants.

acme_dev: Tried toggling to v1 explicitly and reduced max_batch_size to 6. Initial smoke looks better; p99 dropped back to ~250ms. No 400s observed in the next 10 minutes.

opsbot: Incident created: INC-2026-58; priority=P2; owner=@ryan_ml. Links: https://redwood.incidents/INC-2026-58

alex_sre: Long-term fix ideas: 1) add a dimension check at the batching layer to reject/route inconsistent requests (fast fail), 2) annotate model variants with a deterministic batch_key that prevents coalescing across incompatible dims, 3) add a metric for `batch_dim_inconsistency` so we can alert before customer-visible errors.

ryan_ml: Agreed. I'll open a PR to validate dims in the coalescing stage and emit a counter. For quick patch we can also make the runtime prefer strict model_id matching for batching when variants with different output shapes exist.

acme_dev: Thanks all — we'll keep the route pinned and monitor. Please escalate if you see reappears. If helpful, we can share traffic traces (anonymized) for the 3 problematic minutes.

jen_support: Please attach traces if you can. I'll keep the ticket open and update acme_dev when the PR merges. :thumbsup:

ryan_ml: Filed tasks: T-8721 add batch-dim-check; T-8722 add route-level `batch_key` doc. Targeting hotfix rollout tonight to add fast-fail and metric.

acme_dev: One more datapoint — when the spike happened, we also saw a small surge in payload size (longer texts). Could seq_len + mixed quant variants be interacting with batching kernel selection and causing slower drains?

alex_sre: Possibly — longer sequences increase execution time and can amplify tail latency in large coalesced batches. That explains the p99 jump even when not failing. We'll look at batching TTL and kernel selection heuristics in addition to dimension checks.

jen_support: Closing loop: mitigation applied (route pinned + max_batch_size lowered). opsbot: mark INC-2026-58 status=monitoring.

opsbot: Incident INC-2026-58 updated: status=monitoring; assigned=@ryan_ml

acme_dev: Confirmed stabilization for our workload over 30m. Appreciate the quick help.

jen_support: Great — we'll follow up with a postmortem entry summarizing root cause and permanent fixes.
